Disclosure to Promote the Right To Information 

Whereas the Parliament of India has set out to provide a practical regime of right to 
information for citizens to secure access to information under the control of public authorities, 
in order to promote transparency and accountability in the working of every public authority, 
and whereas the attached publication of the Bureau of Indian Standards is of particular interest 
to the public, particularly disadvantaged communities and those engaged in the pursuit of 
education and knowledge, the attached public safety standard is made available to promote the 
timely dissemination of this information in an accurate manner to the public.

SPECIFICATION FOR 
FORCEPS, SPONGE HOLDING, FOERSTER'S 
PATTERN, SMOOTH OR SERRATED JAWS 



1. Scope— Dimensional and other requirements for Foerster's pattern, sponge holding forceps, with 
smooth or serrated jaws used in general surgery. 

2. Shape and Dimensions — As shown in Fig. 1.

FIG. 1 FORCEPS, SPONGE HOLDING, SMOOTH AND SERRATED JAWS, FOERSTER'S PATTERN 

2.1 A deviation of ± 25 percent shall be allowed on all dimensions where otherwise not specified. 

3. Material — Stainless steel shall conform to designation 20CM3 or 30CM3 of IS: 6603 -1972 
c Specification for stainless steel bars and flats '. 

4. Workmanship and Finish 

4-1 The forceps shall be finished smooth and shall be free from burrs, pits, cracks and other surface 
defects.

IS : 10638-1983 

4.2 The movements of the arms of the forceps shall be smooth. 

4.3 The joints shall have no undue play. 

4.4 The working ends shall meet accurately and shall have no side p*ay s 
43 The forceps shall be polished bright and paissivated. 

4.6 All the edges shall be even and rounded off except the serrations. 

5. Heat Treatment — The forceps shall be hardened and tempered to give a hardness of 38® to 430 WV. 

6.. Tests 

6.1 Grip a piece of hard rubber 6 mm thick between the working ends of the forceps. Tighten the grip 
so that the third ratchet engages. Release the grip. At the end of the test the forceps snail show no 
sign of damage. 

6.2 Corrosion Resistance Test — The instrument shall satisfy the boiling and autoclaving test as 
mentioned in IS: 7531 -1975 'Method for boiling ancl autoclaving test for corrosion resistance of 
stainless steel surgical instruments '. 

7. Marking — The forceps shall be marked with the manufacturer's name, initials or recognized trade- 
mark and the words ' Stainless Steel \ 

7A is I Certification Marking — Details available with the Indian Standards Institution. 

8. Packing — Each forceps shall be wrapped in moisture-proof paper and put in cardboard cartons or 
polyethylene bags. They may be packed as agreed to between the purchaser and the supplier.
